```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's payer already spends money on this problem. Patreon's 10% fee plus processing is sourced, and both Reddit quotes show creators actively planning to switch over fees. That is willingness to pay, not just pain. Idea B's demand quotes show frustration with invisible agent work but no evidence that anyone pays to fix it.",
    "Idea A cites a precedent with the same wedge (Starter Story: ~$140K MRR, $3.5M exit) built by a non-technical founder plus one contractor. It also names a concrete low-cash acquisition path: niche community outreach, affiliates, and contests. Idea B has no comparable precedent of a small builder reaching revenue.",
    "Idea B faces a sourced $0 anchor from an incumbent with massive distribution (Slack Code, bundled free into every Slack plan). It also faces a sourced security bar (SOC2, ZDR, SSO) that its own brief says a six-week solo build is unlikely to meet and that is 'plausibly the actual purchase driver.' Its paid channel benchmark (~$650 per devtools SQL) is expensive for a solo operator on a 90-day clock.",
    "Idea B's two load-bearing feasibility claims are flagged [unsourced]: that the product is buildable solo in six weeks, and that demand from non-engineering teams is significant. Under the rules these count as missing, which narrows B to a solo build attempt in a crowded engineering-only niche.",
    "Idea A has real negatives: 0% competitors (Beamly, Ko-fi Free), incumbent dominance of the 'Patreon alternative' search results, and heavy regulatory load (KYC/money-transmitter risk, 1099-K, sales tax). Still, the Memberful model shows a sourced direct-Stripe-account SaaS structure that may reduce that exposure. A 90-day goal needs only one paying creator in one niche, which is a smaller hurdle than one engineering team buying seats over a free bundled alternative."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's claim that 'a thin session-relay + presence/handoff layer is buildable solo in six weeks' is explicitly marked [unsourced], yet the Case For depends on it. The YC Fall 2026 RFS cited as a demand signal has no link. One of the two demand quotes comes from a vendor blog (agentcenter.cloud), so it reads as marketing rather than independent buyer evidence.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with $0-priced competitors, so neither is strong. Idea A's own six-week buildability claim is also unsourced, though not flagged. Its only success precedent depended on a founder with a pre-existing audience, which the brief admits most solo builders lack. Its payments-compliance exposure is a serious risk for one operator with agents. A wins mainly because its demand evidence shows money already being spent and it has a sourced revenue precedent. B's demand evidence stops at pain, and B faces a free incumbent bundle."
}
```
